newsitem.title: USA: AMEX gets set to trade options in 1/16th of dollar.
newsitem.headline: AMEX gets set to trade options in 1/16th of dollar.

text.p: The American Stock Exchange said Wednesday it will be able to process all options trades in minimum increments of 1/16th of a dollar ($0.0625) beginning July 28.
Currently, only options priced below $3 are traded in 1/16ths on all four options exchanges. For options priced above $3, the minimum price increment on premiums is 1/8th.
U.S. stock exchanges have been moving toward trading stocks in the same 1/16th increments.
"Price improvement is every bit as important to the options investor as it is to the equities investor," AMEX chairman Richard Syron said in a statement.
The AMEX added that although its system would be able to handle options trading in 1/16ths on July 28, the industry needed to coordinate the change.
"We are ready to go when the industry is in a position to make this change, but there needs to be cooperation within the options industry," Syron said.
The Chicago Board Options Exchange agreed that the industry must work together on the change.
The exchanges have noted that a starting date for trading all options in 1/16ths has not been set and that regulatory approval would be needed.
In addition, coordination with options quote vendors is needed because options quote traffic is already clogging some communication lines, industry sources said.
"The concern we all have is the capacity of the vendor systems," a spokesman at the Pacific Exchange said.
Michael Schwartz, chairman of the industry's Committee on Options, said the change could "create havoc" with vendors.
"Discussions with the vendor community to adapt to the expanding quote volume is necessary," he said in a recent letter to industry members.
Schwartz is a managing director at Oppenheimer & Co.
